mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases where UNRATE increases by 0.5% or more, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% indicates tighter monetary policy, which may lead to decreased borrowing and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and slowing payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to decreased economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by 0.5% and PAYEMS growth slows below 100,000
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 30% of cases where both UNRATE increases and PAYEMS growth slows, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 indicates supply chain weakness, which may lead to decreased corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases where INDPRO falls below 90, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which may lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of cases where GDPC1 increases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) below 100,000 indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to decreased economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases where PAYEMS growth slows below 100,000, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of slowing real GDP growth (GDPC1) and rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) indicates stagflation, which may lead to decreased corporate margins and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth slows and CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 30% of cases where GDPC1 growth slows and CPIAUCSL increases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 500,000 indicates weak demand in the housing market, which may lead to decreased economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases where HOUST falls below 500,000, this hypothesis is falsified.
